facts.value: Fighter action-state IASA callback with exact signature void ftCo_Run_IASA(Fighter_GObj* gobj). It delegates recognition and state changes to transition predicates and setup routines, using their results only to stop lower-priority processing.
facts.rationale: The matched definition provides the void return and Fighter_GObj pointer parameter. Its body derives the Fighter, invokes action checks, and consumes predicate results through immediate callback returns, which identifies it as an interrupt/action-selection callback rather than a predicate that returns a transition result.

evidence.why: Provides the exact signature, Fighter extraction, delegated transition calls, and void short-circuit control flow.

facts.value: Arbitrates input-driven transitions out of the common Run state in fixed priority order, ending processing as soon as one action checker accepts a transition.
facts.rationale: The complete matched callback consists of an ordered series of transition predicates wrapped in RETURN_IF or followed by explicit returns. Successful dash-attack and guard checks perform setup before returning, while all other successful predicates similarly prevent lower-priority options from being evaluated.

evidence.why: Shows the complete ordered transition chain, setup calls, timer guards, and first-success early returns.
Records acceptance of this complete 300-byte function as a 100% match in PR #1666.

facts.value: Checks transitions in strict short-circuit order: side special; Attack100 input and three additional common attack/catch handlers; dash attack followed by dash-attack move-variable setup; guard activation followed by guard setup using p_ftCommonData->x410; appeal; jump-related handling; then, only when mv.co.run.x0 is nonpositive, a TurnRun-unit transition. If x0 is still positive, processing stops before RunBrake; otherwise RunBrake is checked last. The first successful path ends the callback.
facts.rationale: This sequence follows the matched source literally. RETURN_IF and explicit returns establish first-success semantics, while the paired x0 conditions prove that the final turnaround and RunBrake paths are unavailable until the Run countdown reaches a nonpositive value. Opaque callees are described by their owning subsystem rather than assigned unsupported action names.

evidence.why: Shows every transition predicate in order, dash-attack and guard setup, the x0 gate, and all early returns.

facts.value: Reads the Fighter, its common movement attributes, current ground velocity, controller-derived movement state, and shared common-data constants. getAccelAndTarget produces acceleration and target velocity; the callback may attenuate acceleration using gr_vel / target_vel, writes target_vel multiplied by the common x440 factor to mv.co.run.x4, passes acceleration, target velocity, and ground_friction multiplied by run_dash_turn_friction_multiplier to ftCommon_8007C98C, and then passes the game object to ftCommon_ApplyGroundMovement. Run animation later consumes mv.co.run.x4 when the ground-friction multiplier is below one.
facts.rationale: The relocated physics body preserves the calculation and output flow while exposing the current semantic name run_dash_turn_friction_multiplier for the friction factor formerly described by its placeholder field name. The animation callback still consumes x4 under reduced-friction conditions.

evidence.why: Shows getAccelAndTarget producing acceleration and target velocity and the conditional velocity-ratio attenuation.
Shows the x4 write, current run_dash_turn_friction_multiplier use, common velocity update, and ground-movement call.
Shows Run animation selecting mv.co.run.x4 when the ground-friction multiplier is below one.

facts.value: Per-frame grounded physics callback for the Run state. It computes input-derived acceleration and target velocity, tapers acceleration while the fighter is already moving toward but has not reached that target, records a scaled target for Run animation handling, applies character-specific friction through the common ground-velocity update, and then advances ground movement.
facts.rationale: The current body retains the complete Run physics calculation: target generation, bounded-ratio acceleration taper, cached target write, friction-aware velocity update, and final ground movement. The claim therefore remains sound at the relocated source.

facts.value: On every Run physics update, a nonzero target velocity enables an approach-speed check. If current ground velocity is in the same direction and strictly between zero and the target, acceleration is multiplied by the remaining fractional distance to the target and a shared acceleration factor; otherwise acceleration is left unchanged. The callback always refreshes the Run cached target, performs the common friction-aware velocity update, and applies ground movement, without directly changing action state or processing a timer.
facts.rationale: The relocated body retains the same branch structure: only a nonzero target and a ground-velocity ratio in the open interval zero to one attenuate acceleration, after which all paths reconverge at the cached-target write and common movement calls.

evidence.why: Shows the nonzero-target guard, open-interval ratio test, and conditional acceleration attenuation.
Shows all paths proceeding through the cached-target write, friction-aware velocity update, and ground movement without a state transition or timer.
